tools.name: check_company
tools.description: Check that a company's website is usable for a brief, before spending anything. Pass the domain (acme.com) or any URL on it. Returns the normalised domain, the company name if this company has been seen before (otherwise null), and the credits available. Free: no credit is spent and no brief is star

tools.name: request_brief
tools.description: Start a competitive-intelligence brief for one company. Returns at once with a brief_id; generation takes 3 to 6 minutes. Then call get_brief(brief_id) after poll_after_seconds. Cost: one credit is held now and spent only if the brief is ready with at least one item. An empty or failed brief costs n

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: Get the status of a brief started with request_brief and, once it is ready, the brief. While it is queued or generating, wait poll_after_seconds and call again. Call at most once every 15 seconds per brief. format: markdown (default, ready to relay in chat), json, or html (the full email render). st

tools.name: list_briefs
tools.description: List this account's briefs, newest first, with each brief_id, domain, status and creation time. Briefs are kept for 30 days. Use get_brief(brief_id) to read one.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show this account: credits available, when they expire, credits held by briefs in progress, the limits that apply, how this client is connected (API key or OAuth), and whether it is read-only. Credits are prepaid units, not money; the result carries the credit terms (credits_notice, terms_url). Free

tools.name: get_sample_brief
tools.description: Return a sample of a finished brief, to see what request_brief and get_brief produce. Free, and works without an API key. format: markdown (default, what get_brief relays in chat), json, or html (the full email render). structuredContent always holds the brief as JSON, in the same shape as get_brief

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_brief" stacks urgency/override words (important, always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_company, get_brief, get_sample_brief · Private data: request_brief, get_account, get_sample_brief · Public sink: request_brief, get_brief, get_sample_brief · Destructive: get_brief, get_sample_brief.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_company, get_brief, get_sample_brief · Private data: request_brief, get_account, get_sample_brief · Public sink: request_brief, get_brief, get_sample_brief · Destructive: get_brief, get_sample_brief

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "request_brief" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
